question: The piston rings are placed in the ring groove and provide sealing between which of the following two parts to prevents leakage of high-pressure gases?
solution:
The correct answer is __Piston and the cylinder liner****.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Piston rings__ are essential components in an internal combustion engine.
 
• They are placed in the ring grooves on the outer diameter of the piston.
 
• The primary purpose of the piston rings is to seal the gap between the piston and the cylinder liner.
 
• They prevent the leakage of high-pressure gases from the combustion chamber into the crankcase.
 
• Piston rings also help in heat transfer from the piston to the cylinder liner.
 
• They control oil consumption by scraping excess oil from the cylinder walls.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Piston and Cylinder Head:**
 
 
• The piston does not directly seal the cylinder head; the cylinder head is sealed using a gasket.
 
• The gasket ensures no leakage of gases or fluids between the cylinder head and the engine block.
 
 
 
• **Piston and Cylinder Fins:**
 
 
• The cylinder fins are used in air-cooled engines to dissipate heat, and they are not involved in sealing mechanisms.
 
 
 
• **Piston and Cylinder Block:**
 
 
• The piston does not seal directly against the cylinder block; it operates within the cylinder liner that is fitted into the block.
